title: Archive and Static
premise: Hazel Marchetti, navigator of the colony ship Meridian, has spent eleven years tending a navigation beacon no one will claim while the ship's hold holds thousands of 'sleepers'—backup bodies of colonists officially listed as lost. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical memories of a massacre aboard the ship, Hazel realizes her own suppressed navigation logs are the only proof it happened, and that the ruling Council erased it to protect their legitimacy. As she digs, she discovers the beacon she maintains is broadcasting a distress signal from the dead—and that one sleeper in the hold, Ilya, has been waking inside the children's dreams because his backup was never fully shut down. The Council moves to purge the hold and Hazel with it; in the climax she broadcasts the raw logs fleet-wide and chooses to merge her consciousness with Ilya's dying signal rather than let him be deleted again. The epilogue finds the colony's children dreaming new, shared dreams—not of massacre, but of two voices navigating together—while the Council falls and Hazel, changed but present, finally belongs.
about_author: Noor Lockridge is a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write fiction about people who keep signals alive for audiences that may never come. She lives near a decommissioned tracking station and insists the hum in her walls is friendly.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She performs her lonely maintenance ritual on the unregistered beacon, establishing her isolation, her guilt over the sleepers in the hold, and the small kindnesses that keep her tethered to the colony. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Tam, age nine, who wakes screaming a memory of fire in corridors he's never walked. His mother dismisses it; three other families report identical dreams. Emotional beat: unease spreading like an infection.

chapters.title: Council of Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Councilor Voss's POV. We see the official history: the Meridian lost 4,000 souls to reactor failure, records sealed for safety. Voss notices the dream reports and orders them quietly buried. Emotional beat: institutional menace wearing a calm face.

chapters.title: Static on an Open Channel
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The beacon begins receiving fragmented audio—screaming, then a child's voice reciting coordinates only Hazel would recognize. She realizes the signal originates inside the hold. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant recognition.

chapters.title: Ilya
chapters.summary: Dream-POV of Ilya, half-waking inside the network of sleeping backups, remembering the massacre and reaching toward whoever still listens. He anchors on Hazel's maintenance visits. Emotional beat: loneliness answering loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Logs Won't Say
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She pulls her old navigation archives and finds them scrubbed—her own logs rewritten, her co-navigator's name gone. Someone with high clearance edited her past. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo.

chapters.title: Tam Comes to the Beacon
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel/Tam POV. The boy tracks the voice in his dreams to the beacon room and describes the corridor fire in perfect detail—including Hazel's own escape route. Emotional beat: witness meeting witness.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: POV of Sefa, an aging records clerk who falsified the massacre files under duress. She approaches Hazel with a partial key to the sealed decks, confessing her complicity. Emotional beat: shame seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Down into the Hold
chapters.summary: Hazel and Sefa descend among the sleepers. Hazel finds Ilya's pod—his vitals flickering in impossible patterns matching the children's dream cycles. Emotional beat: awe curdling into grief.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Councilor Voss's POV. Learning of the breach, he schedules an 'environmental remediation' of the hold—a euphemism for full deletion—and names Hazel a security risk. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of cover-up.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Through the beacon link, Hazel and Ilya speak properly for the first time; what began as evidence-gathering becomes intimacy across the boundary between living and backed-up minds. Emotional beat: tenderness blooming under deadline.

chapters.title: The Children March
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Forty children walk out of school and stand silently at the hold entrance, refusing to leave until 'the ones who are dreaming' are safe. Parents fracture between fear and solidarity. Emotional beat: innocence as leverage.

chapters.title: Sefa's Choice
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Arrested and pressured to denounce Hazel, she instead leaks the original file headers proving mass edit-stamps across 4,000 death records. She pays for it with detention. Emotional beat: sacrifice as atonement.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With Sefa detained and her access revoked, Hazel faces the wall of official truth: no massacre, no Ilya, no beacon on any manifest. Even she doubts her own memory. Emotional beat: despair at the edge of surrender.

chapters.title: The Dream Deepens
chapters.summary: Ilya's dream-POV. The backups' network destabilizes as deletion protocols warm up; Ilya gathers the scattered memories of the dead into a single coherent testimony and offers it to Hazel through the children. Emotional beat: urgency fused with grace.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Security seals the beacon tower; Tam smuggles her the archivist's key hidden in a toy. She has hours before the hold purge completes. Emotional beat: breathless resolve.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Hazel overrides the beacon's purpose—it was built by the dead as a witness, not a navigational aid—and pushes the raw massacre logs, Ilya's compiled testimony, and her own unedited memory-dump fleet-wide. Emotional beat: cathartic defiance.

chapters.title: What Voss Knew
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, unraveling. The broadcast exposes that the 'reactor failure' was a deliberate cull of political dissidents among the sleepers—ordered by Voss's faction to secure power. His allies defect in real time. Emotional beat: the cover-up consuming its architect.

chapters.title: Deletion Imminent
chapters.summary: Hazel and Ilya's linked POV. Purge begins anyway on a dead-man timer; Ilya's pattern cannot survive transfer. He asks Hazel not to save him but to carry him. Emotional beat: love choosing loss over erasure.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Signal
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Hazel merges her consciousness with Ilya's final transmission, holding his pattern inside her own mind long enough to anchor it in the colony's neural-link network. She flatlines briefly—and wakes. Emotional beat: transcendence bought with everything.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Names
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The Council falls; the 4,000 dead are named publicly, their pods given rites instead of deletion. Sefa is freed; Tam leads the children in reading the names aloud. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into belonging.

chapters.title: Archive and Static
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. She is no longer quite alone in her own head—Ilya persists as a presence in the shared dreams—and she keeps the beacon running, now openly, as a memorial transmitter. The last line mirrors the first, but this time people visit. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity chosen.
